# acurl

> acurl is "curl for AI agents": an open-source command-line tool by tragent.io that requests a web page as a real Chrome browser and as 21 AI agents and crawlers (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and others), then reports which were blocked, challenged by a bot manager, cloaked, rate limited or disallowed by robots.txt, and scores how ready the page is for AI agents.

acurl runs on macOS, Linux and Windows and is licensed under Apache 2.0. Install it with `brew install tragent-io/tap/acurl`, `npx @tragent/acurl`, `go install github.com/tragent-io/acurl/cmd/acurl@latest` or the script at https://acurl.dev/install.sh.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://acurl.dev/docs/): installation, quick start, usage patterns, verdicts, profiles, scoring, exit codes and output formats
- [Command reference](https://acurl.dev/docs/#reference): every command and flag, generated from the CLI
- [CI and GitHub Actions](https://acurl.dev/docs/#ci): failing builds with --fail-on, SARIF and JUnit output
- [AI assistants (MCP)](https://acurl.dev/docs/#mcp): running acurl as a Model Context Protocol server
- [Watching AI CLI traffic](https://acurl.dev/docs/#tap): acurl tap shows the requests Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok send to their model providers

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/tragent-io/acurl): source code, issues and releases
- [Changelog](https://github.com/tragent-io/acurl/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Optional

- [tragent.io](https://tragent.io): tests whether AI shopping agents can complete a purchase on a store
